title: Canvas element purpose and fallback content
learningObjectives: Explain canvas element purpose and fallback content and create scalable, accessible graphics or media markup.

understand.concept: The canvas element provides a bitmap drawing surface controlled through JavaScript. It can be used for charts, games, and custom graphics. Content inside the canvas element can provide fallback information when canvas is unavailable or when the drawing is not exposed meaningfully.
understand.whyItMatters: Canvas pixels do not automatically provide semantic structure or accessible text. Provide equivalent information and controls in HTML, and keep important data available outside the bitmap.
understand.analogy: Canvas is like a blank drawing board; JavaScript paints pixels onto it, but the drawing itself does not become a structured HTML document.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual vector, bitmap, and accessibility behaviour follows the relevant graphics and browser specifications.

explain.narrative: JavaScript draws three bars. The HTML list provides the same information in an accessible text form.

examples.code:
A bar chart showing values 3, 5, and 8. The data is also listed below.
  • Item A: 3
  • Item B: 5
  • Item C: 8
examples.explanation: JavaScript draws three bars. The HTML list provides the same information in an accessible text form.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered SVG, canvas, or responsive image example.

practise.guidedTask: Create a canvas chart with an equivalent HTML table or list. Explain why the drawing alone is insufficient for all users.
practise.independentTask: Create a small graphic or responsive media example. Include accessible naming or equivalent text and test different display sizes.
hints: Keep important information available as HTML.
Use viewBox for SVG coordinate systems.
Test responsive source selection and image alternatives.

questions.prompt: What should accompany important information drawn only on canvas?
questions.explanation: Canvas pixels do not provide semantic content, so equivalent information should be available in HTML.

questions.prompt: What is a good accessibility practice for meaningful graphics?
options: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.answer: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.explanation: Meaningful visual information must also be available through accessible text or equivalent content.
